subsystems.name: Mycelium scaffold
subsystems.role: fungal threads grow through crop waste or sawdust and bind it into a solid, lightweight matrix.

subsystems.name: Biomineralisation system
subsystems.role: microbes or enzymes precipitate calcium carbonate inside the matrix, hardening it and locking away carbon.

subsystems.name: Protective skin
subsystems.role: stops water ingress and UV damage, and keeps the fungus from resuming growth or rotting later.

subsystems.name: Nutrient and water network
subsystems.role: channels that feed and hydrate a structure that is still living in places.

subsystems.name: Sensing and control layer
subsystems.role: measures moisture, strain and biological contamination so the material can be managed.

subsystems.name: Repair and reprocessing loop
subsystems.role: re-inoculates damaged zones and, at end of life, breaks material down for reuse.

buildSteps.title: Design the form and the biology
buildSteps.detail: The intended shape is modelled computationally, then fungal strains and mineralising microbes are chosen to suit the local climate and feedstock.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the substrate
buildSteps.detail: Agricultural waste or sawdust is sterilised, wetted and packed into moulds or fabric formworks.

buildSteps.title: Grow the hyphal network
buildSteps.detail: Inoculated substrate is kept warm and humid for one to several weeks while hyphae colonise and bind every particle.

buildSteps.title: Harden by biomineralisation
buildSteps.detail: A calcium-rich solution carrying bacteria or enzymes is percolated through the matrix, precipitating calcite crystals between the fibres over days to weeks.

buildSteps.title: Seal the surface
buildSteps.detail: The outer skin is mineralised or coated so the material resists rain, frost and further fungal growth.

buildSteps.title: Assemble modules on site
buildSteps.detail: Blocks and panels are transported, stacked or joined, and the joints are re-inoculated so adjacent pieces fuse into one body.

buildSteps.title: Activate living functions
buildSteps.detail: Capillary water and nutrient lines, sensors and control electronics are threaded through the structure.

buildSteps.title: Commission and maintain
buildSteps.detail: Moisture, strain and contamination are monitored, and cracks or eroded zones are re-grown with fresh culture rather than replaced.

prerequisites.why: grown packaging and acoustic panels are sold today, but structural load-bearing grades are not.
used in trials for soil stabilisation, dust suppression and concrete crack healing, not yet at building scale.
genetically programmed materials that sense, repair or change shape exist in laboratories only.

prerequisites.tech: Durability, fire and moisture data for bio-based structure
prerequisites.why: no long-term evidence exists that a grown wall survives decades of weather, insects and fire.

prerequisites.tech: Standards and certification for living building materials
prerequisites.why: building codes assume inert materials with predictable, testable properties.
the carbon locked into the material must be shown to stay locked for the building's life.

pathway.milestone: non-structural mycelium panels and biocemented ground, plus coral-analogue reef restoration
pathway.unlocks: real production experience and cost data for grown materials.

pathway.milestone: load-light grown blocks and wall systems in low-rise buildings
pathway.unlocks: first certified structural uses and long-term durability records.

pathway.milestone: self-healing modular structures with embedded sensors
pathway.unlocks: buildings that repair their own cracks, cutting maintenance.

pathway.milestone: larger grown districts using local waste as feedstock
pathway.unlocks: construction that stores carbon rather than emitting it, if durability and codes are solved.
